title: The KMT2F histone methyltransferase interacts with the RNA polymerase I machinery to promote ribosomal RNA transcription
experiments_summary: The study employed a broad range of biochemical, cell biological, genomic, and transcriptional methods. (1) Immunofluorescence staining (IFS) was used across multiple cell lines (U-2OS, HEK293, MCF-7, HeLa, IMR90-tert) to examine nucleolar localization of KMT2A and KMT2F, using B23, fibrillarin, and UBF as nucleolar markers; specificity was confirmed by siRNA knockdown and exogenous GFP/dsRed-tagged constructs. (2) Paired-end ChIP sequencing (ChIP-seq) was performed for KMT2A and KMT2F in HEK293 cells using a custom hg38-rDNA genome assembly containing a single annotated rDNA repeat unit; publicly available ChIP-seq datasets for UBF, RNA Pol I, WDR5, WDR82, H3K4me2, H3K4me3, H3K79me2, DOT1L, and controls were analyzed through the same pipeline (FastQC, TrimGalore, Bowtie2, Samtools, DeepTools, IGV). (3) Directed ChIP-qPCR was conducted in HEK293 and IMR90-tert cells using primers spanning the rDNA unit (spacer promoter, 47S core promoter, gene body, termination repeats, intergenic spacer) for KMT2A, KMT2F, RNA Pol I, UBF, H3K4me2, H3K4me3, H3, H3K9ac, H3K9me3, SL1 (TAF1C), RRN3, and KMT2C; canonical loci served as positive/negative controls. (4) Quantitative comparison of ChIP-seq signals versus ChIP-qPCR data was performed by computing RPKM values over primer amplicon coordinates. (5) A genome-wide ChIP-seq distribution analysis segmented the genome into promoters, gene bodies, intergenic regions, and rDNA, and quantified the fraction of ChIP-seq signal for each factor at each compartment using multiBamCoverage and pie chart visualization. (6) In vitro GST pull-down assays were used to test direct protein-protein interactions: bacterially expressed GST-tagged RNA Pol I subunits (RPA12, RPA34, RPA43, RPA49), SL1 subunits (TAF48, TAF63), and hRRN3 were incubated with purified WDR5 (after thrombin cleavage of its GST tag) or with HeLa whole-cell/nuclear extracts, and bound proteins were detected by immunoblotting. GST-KMT2A-SET served as positive control and GST alone as negative control. (7) Endogenous co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) was carried out in mammalian cell lysates using antibodies against KMT2A or KMT2F, and immunoprecipitates were probed for RPA194, UBF, RRN3, and RNA Pol II (Ser2-phosphorylated). (8) S-protein affinity pull-down of SFB-tagged constructs (full-length KMT2F, SET-domain mutant KMT2F N1646A, and RRM fragment spanning residues 74–172) was performed to assess interactions with RNA Pol I subunits and RRN3. (9) RNAi-mediated knockdown (siRNA) of KMT2A, KMT2B, KMT2C, KMT2F, and WDR5 was performed in U-2OS and HEK293 cells; shRNA-mediated stable knockdown of KMT2F and KMT2C was conducted using pLKO.1 vectors transfected via PEI, with scrambled shRNA as control. (10) RT-qPCR was used to quantify pre-rRNA transcription via the 5′ETS region of 47S pre-rRNA, and to measure knockdown efficiency at the mRNA level, using the 2−ΔΔCt method. (11) Complementation assays were performed in stable U-2OS cell lines expressing siRNA-resistant full-length or domain-deleted (ΔSET, ΔTAD) KMT2A or KMT2F proteins; siRNAs targeting 3′UTR or silent-mutation-bearing constructs were used to selectively deplete endogenous transcripts. (12) Pulse-labeling with [32P] orthophosphoric acid was used to measure ongoing rRNA synthesis; labeled RNA was separated on 1.2% agarose gels and visualized by autoradiography/phosphorimaging; 28S rRNA on denaturing formaldehyde-agarose gels stained with ethidium bromide served as a loading control. (13) RNA-seq datasets from KMT2A and KMT2F knockdown versus control conditions (previously published) were re-analyzed using featureCounts and DESeq2; pathway enrichment for ribosome biogenesis-related GO terms was performed using GSEA to assess indirect transcriptional effects. (14) ChIP assays in KMT2F shRNA-knockdown cells were used to measure occupancy of KMT2F, H3K4me2, H3K4me3, H3K9ac, H3K9me3, RNA Pol I, UBF, SL1 (TAF1C), and RRN3 on rDNA; global histone modification levels were assessed by immunoblotting. (15) Rescue ChIP experiments were performed in KMT2F shRNA-background cells expressing wild-type KMT2F or the catalytic dead mutant (N1646A) to determine whether KMT2F's methyltransferase activity is required for RNA Pol I and UBF occupancy at rDNA. (16) Overexpression experiments of KMT2A alone, KMT2F alone, or both in combination were performed, followed by RT-qPCR measurement of rRNA transcripts, to assess synergistic effects on rRNA production.
